project.name: AI-Booster-Kit
project.description: This repository is an agent-agnostic, contract-first synchronization orchestrator for safely coordinating work through separately approved domain adapters. It provides a shareable operating layer for coordinating Jira, GitHub, and Confluence work across multiple coding agents.

nodes.name: model.ts
nodes.summary: Defines the canonical domain types for milestones, work items, execution sets, project profiles, and durable events.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses TypeScript discriminated unions and literal types to constrain workflow vocabulary and host identities.

nodes.name: schema.ts
nodes.summary: Declares AJV schemas for the canonical work artifact, hierarchy records, execution sets, profiles, and event envelopes.
nodes.languageNotes: Builds a typed schema registry from reusable literal constraints and JSON Schema references.

nodes.name: validate.ts
nodes.summary: Compiles the canonical AJV schemas and converts validation failures into precise domain ValidationError instances.
nodes.languageNotes: Maps AJV JSON Pointer paths and constraints into actionable domain errors without losing the failing value type.

nodes.name: envelope.ts
nodes.summary: Creates and validates canonical event envelopes, including stable idempotency keys and exact approved-field checks.
nodes.languageNotes: Derives event identity with a SHA-256 hash over stable business fields while validating the complete envelope.

nodes.name: outbox.ts
nodes.summary: Provides the durable JSONL outbox store for serialized event claims, results, replay protection, and unknown-completion recovery.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses filesystem staging, atomic renames, and per-path operation tails to serialize durable state transitions.

nodes.name: reconcile.ts
nodes.summary: Reconciles an unknown external completion from a read-back result and fails closed when identity or state is ambiguous.

nodes.name: profile.ts
nodes.summary: Loads and strictly validates the local project profile that defines board identity, status vocabulary, and transition mappings.

nodes.name: start-check.ts
nodes.summary: Checks whether implementation may start by requiring traced hierarchy, accepted scope, repository identity, and finalization evidence.

nodes.name: transitions.ts
nodes.summary: Evaluates canonical forward-only board transitions and orthogonal attention states without applying an external mutation.

nodes.name: sync.ts
nodes.summary: Coordinates validated canonical events through allowlist checks, sandbox application, durable claims, read-back verification, and fail-closed outcomes.
nodes.languageNotes: Separates planned, applied, stopped, and unknown outcomes so ambiguous connector behavior cannot be silently retried.

nodes.name: finalize.ts
nodes.summary: Finalizes a canonical milestone into deterministic Jira and Confluence projection intents after validating scope, evidence, and hierarchy.

nodes.name: traceability.ts
nodes.summary: Enforces parent-child hierarchy, unique canonical identifiers, dependency target naming, and allowed board statuses before projection.

nodes.name: domain.test.ts
nodes.summary: Tests canonical domain validation and malformed-record handling across the schema and error boundaries.

nodes.name: e2e.test.ts
nodes.summary: Exercises end-to-end orchestration scenarios including sandbox application, replay, read-back mismatch, tenant safety, and unknown completion.

nodes.name: events.test.ts
nodes.summary: Verifies durable outbox behavior, malformed evidence handling, idempotent replay, claim recovery, and unknown event reconciliation.

nodes.name: lifecycle.test.ts
nodes.summary: Covers profile loading, canonical forward transitions, attention states, start-check evidence, and invalid lifecycle inputs.

nodes.name: planning.test.ts
nodes.summary: Verifies deterministic milestone finalization, canonical artifact replacement, dependency validation, and hierarchy traceability.

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Begin with README.md to understand AI-Booster-Kit as an agent-agnostic, contract-first synchronization orchestrator. Its documentation map and routing-only current-state link establish where the architecture, operating rules, and delivery status are described for the rest of the tour.

tour.title: CLI Entry Point
tour.description: The CLI is the runtime front door, dispatching validation, finalization, synchronization, conformance, and readiness commands. After the project overview, this file shows how user intent enters the system and how errors are reported safely before the deeper layers take over.

tour.title: Contract Compilation
tour.description: The contract layer parses declarative Markdown into a strict canonical vocabulary, capability policy, lifecycle semantics, and stop protocol. The compiler then turns that canonical contract into host-specific projections, making one shared operating model usable across different agent hosts.

tour.title: Domain Model Validation
tour.description: Building on the contract boundary, the domain model defines milestones, work items, execution sets, project profiles, and durable events. AJV-backed validation converts malformed or incomplete data into precise domain errors, keeping later orchestration steps grounded in explicit schemas.
tour.languageLesson: TypeScript types and runtime schemas serve different purposes here: static types guide implementation, while AJV validation protects the boundary when data arrives from files, adapters, or other external inputs.

tour.title: Events and Evidence
tour.description: The event envelope carries canonical operations with stable idempotency keys and exact approved-field checks. Evidence guards sit alongside it to reject empty or credential-like references, connecting the domain model to an auditable execution path without allowing unsafe data into results.

tour.title: Readiness Target
tour.description: The readiness manifest fixes the sandbox target and its tenant, issue, page, repository, commit, and fixture constraints. Observation parsing then defines the safe boundary for Jira, Confluence, GitHub, and traceability evidence, so readiness is evaluated from normalized, validated inputs rather than assumptions.

tour.title: Readiness Decisions
tour.description: The readiness decision engine compares the four-source observations with the canonical manifest and derives a bounded decision. The orchestration wrapper reads an observation bundle through an injected adapter and turns that decision into a readiness certificate, completing the evidence-to-verdict flow introduced in the previous steps.

tour.title: Host Adapter Projections
tour.description: Shared adapter contracts define local event emission, capability reporting, and implementation-start safety checks. The Codex, Claude Code, and Cursor modules provide host metadata to that common machinery, showing how host-specific projections remain aligned without duplicating the domain contract.

tour.title: Operating Model
tour.description: The portable operating model documents the sequence from observation and validation through planning, execution, verification, and handoff, while keeping host and domain rules in their adapters. The Jira-Git-Confluence adapter specializes that model with authority, lifecycle, external-write, audit, and recovery boundaries for the project's synchronization domain.

tour.title: Build and Verification
tour.description: The package manifest defines the Node and validation toolchain, while the strict TypeScript configuration fixes the compilation target and module behavior. GitHub Actions turns those local conventions into repeatable pull-request and main-branch checks, including linting, documentation-link validation, and the test suite.
tour.languageLesson: NodeNext module settings make import and package-boundary behavior explicit; CI then verifies the same project conventions continuously so the contract-first architecture remains reviewable as it changes.
